question: US-Iran 60 day negotiation period extended?
resolution_criteria:
On June 14, 2026, the United States and Iran announced a written diplomatic agreement (the MOU), including a 60-day negotiation period toward a “final deal”, extendable by mutual consent.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if both the United States and Iran publicly and officially announce an extension of the 60-day negotiation period initiated by the MOU between market creation and August 20, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying announcement must be a declarative statement of a present extension of the 60-day negotiation period, a previously-unannounced prior extension of the 60-day negotiation period, or definitive agreement to extend the 60-day negotiation period.

A qualifying announcement must clearly and unambiguously identify an extension of the 60-day negotiation period initiated by the MOU. Statements that merely allude to, reference, or describe an extension, without clearly communicating it, do not qualify. However, the announcement need not use specific terminology or reference the MOU by name.

A qualifying announcement must be made through official channels, by an individual acting in an official capacity. Statements made incidentally or informally in a context not intended for official communication do not qualify.

The extension must be mutually announced by the United States and the Islamic Republic of Iran by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Mutual announcement means that taken together, the announcements from the United States and the Islamic Republic of Iran directly indicate that both parties have agreed to extend the 60-day negotiation period, or have recognized a definitive extension of the period.

The following do not qualify as official announcements: 
- Anonymous, unattributed, or leaked statements not confirmed as official; 
- Statements by persons not authorized to speak for the United States or Iran;
- Third-party speculation, analysis, or predictions that the United States or Iran will announce or implement an extension of the 60-day negotiation period; 
- Satirical, fabricated, hacked, or impersonated communications; 
- Statements that describe a prospective, contingent, probable, or conditional extension of the 60-day negotiation period rather than announcing a present and decided position.

Once an extension has been mutually announced by the United States and Iran, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether it is later reversed, or whether the extension is ever actually implemented.

Resolution will be based on official information from the United States and Iran, including their official representatives.
research:
I couldn't find any official US or Iranian announcement extending the MOU's 60-day period as of August 7. The US declared the MOU over in early July, and Iran formally suspended it on July 18. I've left out everything dated after August 7, as you asked.

## 1. Resolution source
- No single URL is named. The question resolves on official statements from both the US government (White House, State Department) and Iran (Foreign Ministry, President's office). I could not open several primary pages because the proxy refused the connection.
- 2026-06-14: The US and Iran announced the MOU. The text commits both sides to "negotiating and achieving the final deal in a maximum 60 days, extended with mutual consent." Signing is reported as June 17 or 18, so the 60 days end about mid-August, just before the market's August 20 cutoff. [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/06/17/middleeast/us-iran-war-mou-text-intl), [CBS](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/us-iran-deal-memorandum-of-understanding-text/), [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/06/14/us-iran-ceasefire-extended-hormuz-reopen-trump)
- Latest status: I found no joint or matching extension announcement through 2026-08-07.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet, but the framework has broken down. Both sides have said the MOU is dead or suspended, which makes a formal mutual extension less likely.
- 2026-07-08: Trump said the MOU was "effectively over" after Iranian attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. US Central Command reportedly struck more than 80 targets in Iran, and the US reimposed oil sanctions. [Asiae](https://view.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026070818080928025), [Naked Capitalism](https://www.nakedcapitalism.com/2026/07/iran-war-trump-declares-mou-over-after-biggest-us-iran-exchange-of-strikes-since-signing-in-struggle-over-strait-of-hormuz-control-us-suspends-iran-oil-sanction-waiver.html)
- 2026-07-18: Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi announced that Iran had suspended its MOU commitments because of "US violations." ProPakistani reports he said Iran would not start negotiations under any circumstances. Spokesman Baghaei said the MOU had "effectively been suspended." [ProPakistani](https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/18/iran-suspends-islamabad-mou/), [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2026/7/18/iran-accuses-us-of-striking-critical-infrastructure-as-war-intensifies), [Oman Observer](https://www.omanobserver.om/ampArticle/1193032)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-04: Al Jazeera reports that Baghaei said no talks with the US were under way, only technical discussions with Oman on reopening Hormuz. He still called Pakistan "the mediator," with Qatar available if needed. Pakistan has invited senior Iranian officials as it tries to revive mediation. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/4/can-pakistan-keep-us-iran-diplomacy-alive-as-mistrust-deepens)
- 2026-07-14: Al Jazeera reports trust has broken down again and asks whether Pakistan can bring the two sides back to talks. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/14/with-us-iran-trust-broken-again-can-pakistan-bring-them-back-to-talks)
- 2026-07-08 to 07-18: The largest exchange of strikes since the MOU was signed. Iran says at least 50 people were killed by US strikes in July. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2026/7/18/iran-accuses-us-of-striking-critical-infrastructure-as-war-intensifies)
- June 2026 (exact date unclear): Speaking in Paris, Trump said the 60 days were "not a hard deadline," that talks "could take longer," and that he was open to extending if Iran was serious. This is a conditional statement, so it would not count under the rules. [Just the News](https://justthenews.com/government/white-house/president-trump-says-60-day-timeline-iran-memorandum-not-hard-deadline-peace), [WDEF](https://www.wdef.com/?p=2488119)

## 4. Base rates
- I found no clean base rate. In past US-Iran talks, deadlines were often stretched or extended. The JPOA (Joint Plan of Action) was formally extended in July and November 2014, and the 2015 Lausanne deadline slipped past March 31 ([NPR](https://www.npr.org/sections/thetwo-way/2015/03/31/396561443/deadline-day-arrives-for-iran-nuclear-talks)). Those extensions came while talks were still running and both sides were complying. That is not the case now, with the MOU suspended and strikes resuming.
- The rules require official declarations from both sides. Mediator reports from Pakistan or Qatar, or leaks, do not count, which is a high bar.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket has a market titled "US-Iran 60 day negotiation period extended?" that expires August 20 ([Orrery](https://orrery.me/markets/us-iran-60-day-negotiation-period-extended-20260624044855448), [CoinGape](https://coingape.com/prediction-markets/will-us-iran-60-day-negotiation-period-be-extended/)).
- A Pythia newsletter says the market traded between 40% and 73% over its life, then fell to the mid-20s around 2026-08-06 ([Pythia](https://pythia.beehiiv.com/p/new-post-5e95)). I could not open that page to confirm the figure.
- An undated CoinGape snapshot showed 62%, and another aggregator showed 48%. Both are probably older.
- I found no Kalshi or Manifold market on this exact question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- About 2026-08-13 to 08-17: the 60-day window ends, depending on whether it is counted from June 14 or from the June 17/18 signing. Expect official statements around then.
- Pakistan's renewed mediation, including its invitation to senior Iranian officials, and a possible Qatari channel.
- Fighting, new sanctions or Hormuz incidents could harden positions further. Iran's line so far is that no talks are taking place.
- To resolve Yes, both governments must officially confirm an extension by 2026-08-20, 11:59 PM ET.
